correctness.rationale: The defined loopless overlap adjacency yields exactly diagonal-star triangles and two cyclic off-diagonal triangles per 3-letter subset, with no tetrahedra. Each diagonal-star subcomplex is a cone; pairwise intersections are edges and triple intersections empty, so its union is homotopy K_q. The two cyclic triangles per unordered triple attach along the same triangular graph cycle. One of each kills the entire free π1 integrally; the triangular boundaries through a root generate the primitive integral cycle lattice of rank binom(q-1,2). The kernel of the signed boundary is free of rank 2 binom(q,3)-binom(q-1,2), and simply connected 2-dimensional Whitehead/Hurewicz yields the stated wedge. The boundary q=2 is an interval. Independent face census and mod-two chain computations for q=2..8 checked triangle types, dimension bound, face count and Betti ranks; finite data are used only as corroboration.

value.rationale: The two-letter full-alphabet de Bruijn graph is a fundamental natural finite word-overlap family, so determining its entire integral clique-complex homotopy is a motivated structural classification. The result explains exactly how the large original graph-cycle lattice is killed by local overlap triangles and how an explicit cubic number of integral two-sphere classes survives, with q=3 as the first noncontractible case. The claim is not merely a short combinatorial count or field homology table: it identifies the fundamental group and all integral homotopy type for every alphabet size, providing a baseline for topological word-network models.
